wire.errors.session_host.unsupported.role: engage refusal shown in place of a started session when the platform has no launchd-style service manager
wire.errors.session_host.unsupported.tone: plain, calm, and final: say the session did not start and nothing was changed. No blame.
wire.errors.session_host.unsupported.note: The session host is Local Operator's own background process that starts session runtimes so they keep running when the app or terminal closes. 'service manager' means launchd on macOS. Keep it a single sentence pair; do not name launchd or any command.

wire.errors.session_host.unavailable.role: engage refusal when the session host could not be reached in time
wire.errors.session_host.unavailable.tone: plain and reassuring; the remedy is to retry shortly.
wire.errors.session_host.unavailable.note: 'session host' is the product term for the background process; translate it consistently as a noun phrase, not as a person or a server. The session was NOT started, so a retry is safe.

wire.errors.session_host.refused.role: engage refusal when the session host answered but declined to start the session
wire.errors.session_host.refused.tone: plain; one retry, then point at the log.
wire.errors.session_host.refused.note: logs/session-host.log is a literal relative path and must stay verbatim; 'Local Operator folder' is the user's Local Operator data folder.
